title: How species evolve
description: A phylogenetic tree of one product: time runs top to bottom, 🌿 alive, ☠ extinct, 🦴 fossil

blocks.title: S0 · founder
blocks.details:
**Genotype:** no genes, the product as it is today.

**Fate:** extinct. Once its children S1 and S2 proved themselves, traffic flowed to them and S0 stopped getting new users. Nobody had to decide to switch it off.

There is no control version: S0 was never special, only the first.

blocks.title: Fossil
blocks.details: **Optional.** A frozen copy of the founder kept on 1–2% of traffic. It never reproduces and never competes; it only gives an absolute reference point ("are we better than where we started?") and helps catch seasonality.

blocks.title: S1
blocks.details:
**Genotype:** onboarding gene, allele B.

**Fate:** alive, 25% of traffic. A successful parent: it produced S3 by mutation and S4 by crossing. It lives side by side with its children, so they are compared with it (genealogical control).

blocks.title: S2
blocks.details:
**Genotype:** pricing page gene, allele A.

**Fate:** extinct. Its weight decayed and it lost its slot. But its genes did not have to die with it: the pricing gene passed to S4 by crossing.

The unit of selection is the **gene**, not the species. Species are temporary carriers.

blocks.title: S3
blocks.details:
**Genotype:** onboarding B + checkout copy gene.

**Fate:** lethal mutation. The checkout copy broke a guardrail metric (payment errors). The fast guardrail path killed S3 within minutes and its users went back to the closest living relative, S1.

The checkout gene's score drops; a skill opens a PR that deletes its code.

blocks.title: S4 · leader
blocks.details:
**Genotype:** onboarding B + pricing page A.

**Fate:** alive, 73% of traffic and growing. Both genes keep winning across every species that carries them, so the regression gives them high fitness.

Next: the onboarding gene is **fixed** — merged into the base, its flag removed. From then on it is simply part of the product, and the slot is free for new mutations.
